steps.name: What the requests actually do
steps.text:
About 85% of requests read (menus, restaurant listings, order status) and about
12% write (placing and updating orders). Reads dominate, and most read the same
few hundred restaurants.

steps.name: Where the database time goes
steps.text:
The database is the slowest component even at current load: 115ms of the 250ms
is spent there, and it rises sharply as utilisation climbs. Write capacity on
the current tier is only slightly below read capacity.

steps.name: Add an application server
steps.text:
Application capacity increases. Database load increases with it — every new
server sends its own traffic to the same database.

steps.text:
Traffic can now be distributed across application servers. Until this exists,
extra servers sit idle. Session state held in a server's memory will now break.
